thread:
Harpreet: Quick sync from the edge customer workshop. They run inference in constrained on-prem appliances that are intermittently disconnected. Current client_pin model assumes online control-plane; we need an "offline-safe" pin manifest format so edge nodes can make deterministic resolver decisions without constant control-plane connectivity.
Jules: +1. We also need small deltas because the appliances are bandwidth-sensitive. Idea: signed manifest with optional delta_base and explicit TTL.
Marcos: sketching a manifest schema here (pseudo-JSON pasted for clarity):
```json
{
  "manifest_id": "m-2026-03-01:0001",
  "manifest_version": 2,
  "delta_base": "m-2026-02-15:0078", // optional
  "issued_at": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-03-08T12:00:00Z",
  "scope": "tenant|app|route",
  "pins": [
    {"route":"/v1/embedding","model":"embed-v3","hash":"sha256:...","pin_type":"hard","precedence":100}
  ],
  "compatibility": ["kv-cache-safe","quantized-8bit"],
  "signature": "ed25519:...",
  "compress":"zstd-9"
}
```
Harpreet: Key requirements from ops: 1) deterministic tie-breaking offline; 2) ability to apply compact delta diffs; 3) signed manifests so nodes reject replayed/old pins; 4) clear expiry so stale manifests dont stick.
Jules: For deterministic tie-breaking propose fields: (a) manifest_version (monotonic), (b) precedence numbers on pins, (c) controller_id fallback when precedence ties (lexicographic). Edge resolver algorithm: pick highest precedence pin that is not expired and for which model compatibility tags match local runtime. If none, fall back to fallback_hint in manifest or use local default.
Marcos: Delta encoding rules: if delta_base present, node should fetch full manifest only if its missing base. Deltas are relative edits (add/remove pins, update TTLs). We use a small op format to keep diffs compact. Also compress.
Harpreet: Security: signatures required for any manifest that modifies or creates hard pins. Soft pins can be allowed unsigned with lower precedence but must be clearly labeled. Also add a revocation manifest nonce list so control plane can revoke a previously-signed manifest; nodes should check nonce list at next connectivity window.
Jules: telemetry: nodes emit manifest.apply.{success,fail,reject} with tags {tenant,manifest_id,reason}. Also manifest.staleness.gauge to track fraction of nodes with expired manifests.
Marcos: UX notes: Console should show manifest lineage graph and allow generating deltas between manifests. SDKs: expose manifest_id and manifest_source in API responses and provide a small manifest-apply log.
ops-bot: canary deploy queued: resolver-edge-manifests -> staging. ETA 20m. :rocket:
Harpreet: Next steps: create RFC follow-up that defines precise op-diff format, signature verification rules, and revocation semantics. Jules: I can write the deterministic resolver pseudocode. Marcos: Ill prototype a zstd+op-diff encoder for the control plane. If staging goes well, we'll run a limited customer canary on 10 appliances.
